newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols off peaks but remain edgy.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols off peaks but remain edgy.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options were off peaks but still hovering nervously at very rich levels as the dollar clawed back above 113.50 yen in the U.S. after diving to 112 overnight, dealers said.
Uncertainty about the outcome of today's ongoing Federal Open Market Committee meeting was also keeping the market on its toes, they added.

"Volatilities have been bid aggressively, not so much because people want to make profit out it but because of desperate short-covering," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.
"Market-makers are passing on stuff to somebody else like rugby balls, just trying not to get caught," he said.

Traders noted that interbank dealers were collectively short gamma and vega due to swelling end-user demand for options. The dollar's nosedive has also wiped out a lot of exotic options, leaving dealers short in the plain vanillas, which had been meant as theta hedge for the exotics.
The dollar has fallen more than 15 yen after peaking at 127.46 yen on May 1, inflicting acute pain on any short volatility positions, particularly those in gamma-rich short dates.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility was assessed at 14.5/14.9 percent, up about 2.5 point on the day and about 6.0 point above where it was at the start of the month.

Because a number of what had seemed like very low barrier prices for long-range exotics were broken, buy-back of longer-dated hedges boosted the back end, which tend to be much slower to move. Six-month and one-year gained about 1.2 point each to 11.4/11.6 and 11.1/11.3 percent respectively.
A U.S. bank trader said the volatility curve was likely to stay inverted for a while as the market determines if spot would stabilize after the FOMC or head toward 1995 lows.
"Even if they did raise rates, I don't think that's going to change the trend here right away," he said.
Traders said the dollar tended to meet heavy selling pressure each time it tried to make a significant rebound. So far today, the high-113 yen area appeared to be strong resistance.
"The lack of any significant correction in the dollar's recent decline shows just how people had been content with unhedged long dollar positions for quite some time," Okada at DKB noted.
Dollar/mark volatilities were also higher, but to a much lesser extent as the spot dollar stayed within well traveled ranges, holding well at support in the mid-1.68 mark area.
One-month implied volatility rose to 9.8/10.1 percent from Monday's 9.2/9.4.
The dollar's resilience against the mark in the face of the dollar/yen plunge could be a sign that dollar/mark's next major move would be to the upside, traders said.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal, the put/call pricing differential, stood at 0.1/0.4 point in favor of mark calls in dollar/mark and 1.2/1.6 skewed for yen calls in dollar/yen.
